clue.text: Clergyman has a beer in musical play

parts.note: a pastor is a minister in charge of a congregation
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A vicar sits with a pint at the theatre during a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastorale is a stage work or composition on rustic shepherd themes, often set to music.

clue.text: The problem of knotted ropes

indicators.note: ropes that are knotted are tangled up, so their letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: The difficulty with ropes is that they get tangled.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question or difficulty, a tricky problem.

clue.text: Veteran keeps motor vehicle in Norway

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one word is held inside the other

parts.note: an old stager is a veteran; stager alone means an experienced hand
a van is a motor vehicle

explanation.surface: An old hand still owns a car while living in Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Stavanger is a port city on the south-west coast of Norway.

clue.text: Duos expire tragically in Greek play

indicators.note: tragically suggests things going badly wrong, so the letters of these two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Pairs of characters die in a classical tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tragically' fits the surface of a Greek tragedy, but it is the anagram signal for DUOS EXPIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus Rex is the tragedy by Sophocles, a classic drama of ancient Athens.

clue.text: Satisfy primate by feeding with vegetables

indicators.note: feeding a creature with something puts that food inside it

parts.note: an ape is a primate
peas are vegetables

explanation.surface: Keep a monkey happy by giving it greens.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease someone is to pacify or placate them, meeting their demands.

clue.text: Vulnerable former model died

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to pose is to model for an artist or photographer
d is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A one-time catwalk model has passed away, poor thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exposed means being open to attack or harm, unprotected.

clue.text: One gets in a tizzy in mid-flight

indicators.note: gets in means enters, so the single letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a stir is a commotion or fuss, a tizzy
a means one, as in a dozen eggs

explanation.surface: A nervous flyer panics halfway through the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel, but it is a flight of steps; a single step is found anywhere along one.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is one step, which sits partway up a flight of steps.

clue.text: Fusses over a drink

indicators.note: over in a down clue signals turning the word upside down, so it is read backwards

parts.note: ados are fusses, as in much ado

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss about a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy soft drink or mixer.

clue.text: Knight enters sector of the battle field

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so the letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: an area is a sector or zone
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A mounted warrior rides into part of a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of combat or contest, like a gladiatorial ring.

clue.text: Term loosely embracing a type of artist

indicators.note: embracing means holding within its arms, so one part goes inside the other
loosely means not fixed in place, so the letters of the word are shuffled

parts.note: a brand is a type or make of product

explanation.surface: An art term used vaguely to cover a kind of painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' makes REMT, which 'embracing' then wraps round the type of product; 'Term' looks like a word about art, but it is only the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was the great Dutch painter of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Cope with team leader stranded in desert

indicators.note: stranded in means stuck inside, so the letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: sand is what a desert is made of

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A team captain left alone in the desert has to survive.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate or bear it.

clue.text: Philip and Edward are getting paper that's fancy

parts.note: Pip is a short form of Philip, as in Great Expectations
Ed is a short form of Edward
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Two men buy some stationery that is rather elaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is an unrealistic hope, a mere fancy or fantasy.

clue.text: Obtain applause for review, again

parts.note: to reap is to gain or obtain, as the harvest of one's efforts
praise is acclaim or applause

explanation.surface: A show earns a fresh round of clapping when critics look again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappraise is to assess once more, revising an earlier judgement.

clue.text: Pretty loud voice

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
to air an opinion is to voice it

explanation.surface: Someone attractive has a booming way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in its old sense means beautiful, as in fair maiden.

clue.text: Albert to contemplate a mountain range

parts.note: to watch is to observe or contemplate
a chain is a line of mountains

explanation.surface: A man named Albert gazes at the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Albert' looks like a man's name but is the word for a type of watch chain, named after Prince Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: An albert is a heavy chain for a pocket watch, worn across a waistcoat, popularised by Prince Albert.

clue.text: Respected English circus clown

parts.note: august means venerable or highly respected

explanation.surface: A distinguished English performer works as a clown in the big top.
explanation.definitionFit: An auguste is a type of clown in red-nosed, clumsy costume, the foil to the whiteface.

clue.text: Satan devastated land mass of Russian royal

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the letters of the word are scattered into a new order

parts.note: Asia is the largest continental land mass

explanation.surface: The Devil lays waste to a continent belonging to a Tsar's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anastasia was the youngest daughter of Tsar Nicholas II, a grand duchess of Russia.

clue.text: Inscrutable clergyman entertains a displaced person

indicators.note: entertains means plays host to, so the guest letters are held inside the word

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman
DP is the abbreviation for displaced person, a refugee

explanation.surface: A stony-faced cleric gives hospitality to a refugee.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face shows no emotion, impossible to read.

clue.text: Fuming when conduit's stolen

parts.note: piping is a system of pipes, a conduit; the 's means is
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Someone is furious that their pipework has been nicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping hot means extremely hot, steaming, as fuming food might be.

clue.text: Is earl's disposition stuffy?

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Is a nobleman's temperament rather pompous?
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' reads as temperament, but it is the anagram signal in its sense of arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An airless room lacks fresh air and is close and stuffy.

clue.text: Winger has fight on the terrace

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do
a row of houses is a terrace in British usage

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing gets into a scrap with the fans in the stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer but means something with wings, a bird. A British terrace is a row of joined houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small bird, and birds fly on wings.

clue.text: Lift up a stone in the control een tre

parts.note: to cock is to raise or tilt upwards, as an ear or a hat
a pit is the stone of a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone hoists a rock at mission headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockpit is where a pilot sits, the place from which an aircraft is controlled.

clue.text: Northern comic supports Greek character in conversation

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a wag is a joker or comic

explanation.surface: A comedian from the north backs a Greek actor in a dialogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal chat, a gossip.

clue.text: Quaint hairstyle disguises oriental

indicators.note: disguises means conceals, so the word sits concealed within the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned coiffure hides someone from the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai describes something from Thailand, in East Asia.

clue.text: Revive a late party

parts.note: a wake is a gathering held for the late, someone who has died

explanation.surface: Bring someone round with a party late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' suggests the hour, but it means dead: a wake is held for the deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: To awake is to rouse or bring back to consciousness.

clue.text: Painting Olga on acid is disastrous

indicators.note: disastrous means a terrible mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A painting of Olga under the influence of LSD is a catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: La Gioconda is the Italian title of Leonardo's Mona Lisa.

clue.text: In time soldier gives consent

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the soldier goes inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier in crosswords

explanation.surface: In due course a serviceman says yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to assent or say yes to something.

clue.text: Most important metal

definitions.meaning: the ... role or story is the principal, foremost one
a heavy grey metallic element, chemical symbol Pb

explanation.definitionFit: The lead item is the main one, and lead is also the soft heavy element.

clue.text: Pest controller succeeded with triumph after trouble

indicators.note: after places the piece for triumph behind the piece for trouble

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
care is worry or trouble
to crow is to boast in triumph

explanation.surface: A rat-catcher won through, exulting after some difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pest controller' suggests an exterminator, but it is the figure in a field that frightens birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow is a dummy set in fields to keep birds off the crops.

clue.text: Hate sailor initially having gold

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A seaman detests owning precious metal at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to loathe or detest.

clue.text: Change the last word, Penny!

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer
d is the old British abbreviation for a penny, from the Latin denarius

explanation.surface: Someone tells Penny to alter the final word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman addressed by name, but it is D, the pre-decimal British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to alter or correct, typically a text.

clue.text: Engineer recovers lost energy for transport

indicators.note: recovers read as re-covers means covers over, so one word is wrapped round the other

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine
gone means lost or missing
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A mechanic gets back power that went missing in the vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recovers' looks like regains, but read as re-covers it means wraps round; 'Engineer' looks like an anagram signal but is a famous Scottish inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagonette is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a form of transport.
